items.title: Coordination records require no correlating identity
items.statement: The only universally required field is schema_version while project, run, agent, event, operation, revision, and idempotency fields are optional. A conforming event can therefore be impossible to route, correlate, deduplicate, order, or attribute to the advertised key family.
items.impact: Unattributable records can corrupt coordination state or be silently discarded without a schema violation.

items.title: Named event variants lack variant payload and transition invariants
items.statement: Registration, status, operation, ownership, unregister, crash, abort, and export are multiplexed into one key_shape, but no discriminator field is required and no per-variant payload, predecessor state, terminal-state rule, or legal transition table is defined.
items.impact: Consumers cannot distinguish legal state changes from malformed or contradictory transitions.

items.title: Replay guarantees rely on optional controls
items.statement: Replay claims idempotency keys and expected revisions prevent duplicate or stale updates, yet both controls are optional. The contract gives no fallback when either is absent and therefore does not make its own replay guarantee enforceable.
items.impact: Duplicate delivery and racing writers can produce divergent projections while remaining schema-conforming.

dimension_assessments.summary: Authority-sensitive legacy mirror callers are anticipated by the reopen condition but absent from the declared consumer inventory.
Event variants have no required discriminator, payload shape, transition table, or terminal-state invariants.
Optional revision and idempotency fields plus undefined ordering and identity reuse leave duplicate, stale-write, ownership, and ABA races.
Projection/checkpoint and mirror-export commit boundaries, poison-event behavior, and crash states are undefined.
Rebuildability is asserted, but rollback, partial-batch recovery, migration rollback, and compensation for destructive lifecycle events are unspecified.
Broad producers lack emission permissions and authoritative consumers lack a computable freshness gate.
Retention, erasure, compaction, path-hash privacy, and metadata disclosure rules remain incomplete despite explicit secret exclusions.
Legacy file inputs and mirror output paths lack validation, provenance, confinement, size, and quarantine contracts.
Inspection views receive projections without required lag, loading, partial, error, quarantine, or authority indicators.
Platform-hook and storage outages have no buffering, retry, reconciliation, gap-detection, or safe refusal behavior.
No cardinality, lag, batch, retention, compaction, memory, or backpressure limits constrain high-churn coordination data.
The authoritative core is a machine storage-value registry, not an interaction contract; inspection-view accessibility remains a presentation-owner concern.
No user-facing strings or locale-dependent values are prescribed by these machine encodings; localization remains outside this storage window.
Legacy import/cutover and mixed-version reader-writer behavior are not specified.
Required operational signals for lag, replay, rejection, divergence, retention pressure, and reader refusal are absent.
Abort, unregister, and crash transitions lack authorization, preconditions, compensation, and ownership-release ordering; mirror deletion itself is explicitly safe for canonical history.
Deferred self-references and downstream owner links lack a machine-testable gate ensuring payload schemas precede authoritative callers.
No executable or deterministic oracle tests replay, concurrency, crash recovery, migration, redaction, freshness, or non-authority claims.
Identifier lifetime and reuse, canonical ordering domains, and closure of deferred placeholder schemas remain unresolved sources of emergent failure.
